examples.knowledge_point: Computing a Conditional Probability Over an Interval
examples.problem:
| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.2$ | $0$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.1$ | $0.05$ | $0.15$ | $0$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.2$ | $0.05$ | $0$ | $0.1$ |

Compute $P(0\lt Y \lt 3\,|\, X=0  )$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above. Round your answer to two decimal places.
examples.worked_solution:
By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0<Y<3\,|\,X=0) & =\frac{P((0<Y<3),X=0)}{P(X=0)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=0,(0<Y<3))}{P(X=0)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=0,Y=1)+P(X=0,Y=2)}{P(X=0)} \\  & =\frac{f(0,1)+f(0,2)}{{f}_{X}(0)},\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_X(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(0) & =f(0,0)+f(0,1)+f(0,2)+f(0,3) \\  & =0.2+0+0.05+0.1 \\  & =0.35.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(0,1)=0$ and $f(0,2)=0.05.$ 

Finally, substituting our values into the formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0<Y<3\,|\,X=0) & =\frac{f(0,1)+f(0,2)}{{f}_{X}(0)} \\  & =\frac{0+0.05}{0.35} \\  & =\frac{0.05}{0.35} \\  & ≈0.14.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=3$ | $Y=5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=2$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.15$ | $0.05$ | $0.15$ |
| $X=6$ | $0.2$ | $0$ | $0.05$ |

Compute $P(X=4\,|\,Y=3)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above. Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
feedback.worked_solution:
By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by

$$
P(X=4\,|\,Y=3)=\frac{P(X=4,Y=3)}{P(Y=3)}=\frac{f(4,3)}{{f}_{Y}(3)},
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(3) & =f(2,3)+f(4,3)+f(6,3) \\  & =0.1+0.05+0 \\  & =0.15.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(4,3)=0.05.$ 

Finally, substituting ${f}_{Y}(3)=0.15$ and $f(4,3)=0.05$ in our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=4\,|\,Y=3) & =\frac{f(4,3)}{{f}_{Y}(3)} \\  & =\frac{0.05}{0.15} \\  & =0.33.\end{aligned}
$$
